verdict: Caution: lend to established Surat polishers with a verified order book and clean parcel-level stock records; decline job-work units, sub-₹5-crore-scale newcomers, and anything collateralised only by bourse premises.
title: Surat Cut & Polished Diamonds: a note to the credit manager
narrative:
## What the business physically is
Surat cuts and polishes natural diamonds and, increasingly, grows and cuts lab-grown ones; what leaves the city is loose polished stones sold to dealers and manufacturers, not finished jewellery [9]. **A polishing unit is a conversion shop: rough comes in on near-cash terms, is converted at the bench in days, and goes out as graded parcels to a few known foreign buyers.** Surat's airport handled no international freight in FY2025-26, so parcels are cleared locally and flown from Mumbai [9] — transit time is real and cash sits in it. The skill base runs to lakhs of workers across the ecosystem [2].

## Where value and cash sit
**Value sits in the rough parcel and the sealed polished parcel, not in the bench or the building.** Machines are cheap and replaceable; inventory is the whole business, and it is movable, re-gradable and hard to value on recall. Pricing power sits with the overseas buyer; the polisher is a price-taker on thin per-carat margins. For yield, days of rough stock, days of finished stock and credit given to buyers: collect from customer. Retail peers show how slowly stone inventory turns — about 1.1 stock turns in stores averaging 11–12 months old against a 2.5–3 mature-store target [6] — so treat any proposal that assumes fast stock liquidation on enforcement as optimistic.

## What has changed — local news first
The two freshest local reports contradict each other and both are worth reading. One (30 Oct) reports advance Christmas orders and a Diwali break cut to 15 days, with units running to 5 November [2]; the other (29 Oct) reports closures stretched to 25 days from 15, and about 300 small units shut in six months [4]. **One fact sits under both: work is flowing to units holding confirmed export orders, while subcontracted small units have already gone dark.** Separately, the ₹3,200-crore Surat Diamond Bourse has roughly 300 of 4,200 offices operational nearly three years after inauguration, and it was privately funded, not state-funded [1][3]. So when a proposal lands, check what the bourse premises are being offered as; if they are the collateral story, ask what the unit's own order book is.

## Peer results and rating reports — different businesses, read for texture
Listed jewellery retailers are not Surat polishers, but their numbers show where stone demand lives. One peer grew Q2 revenue 17% to ₹121 crore with diamond-stone volume up 28%, and over 95% of its book is design jewellery using smaller stones against 4–5% solitaires [5]. Another reports diamond jewellery up 21% by value and 11% by volume, with stud ratio at 11.9% [6]. The certification business grew Q2 profit 43% on lab-grown volumes at 61% EBITDA margin [7]. R.Rajesh Exports carries [ICRA]BB(Stable)/[ICRA]A4 [8] — that report is undated in my folder, treat it as old and re-verify. Bank credit is running +33.0% YoY against output +3.8%, a gap of +29.2 pp [D]; that is the competition you are lending into, not a demand signal. Gujarat's GST is +11.9% Apr-to-date against India's +6.1% [D] and electricity demand +11.0% against +9.5% [D], with IIP NIC 32 at +3.2% [D]. **Local consumption is healthy and almost irrelevant here — a Surat polisher's cash is decided in the US and China** [1][4]. Note the 50% US tariff reference is from a page last updated 25 August 2025 [9]; confirm today's duty with the customer.

## Where the growth is, and who to avoid
- Pursue mid-size polishers with their own bench, confirmed December Christmas orders [2], buyer-wise export realisation on file, and part of the book in lab-grown with written CVD/HPHT method and treatment disclosure per parcel [9].
- Pursue order-backed and receivable-backed limits; the invoice and the shipping bill are the security, not the loose stone.
- Avoid pure job-work units for others, units under three years, anyone whose plan assumes a shift to the bourse [1][3], and single-buyer China exposure [4].

## How to grow safely
**Structure as LC-backed or bill-discount limits against confirmed orders, with a stock ceiling and a named grader.** Take every month: parcel-wise stock statement with grading, bank statements, export realisation and shipping bills, buyer-wise sales, payroll and bench attendance, electricity bill. Covenant peak stock days, a cap on unhedged rough purchased, DSCR, and a bar on related-party rough purchases. Verify stock quarterly with our own valuer, not the borrower's.

## Early warnings to act on
Use the triggers in the watchlist; the point is that in this trade the first sign is a quiet bench, not a bounced cheque.
watch: two weeks with no fresh rough purchase while payroll still runs -> stop fresh disbursement and physically inspect stock
finished-stock days rising while billing is flat -> move the account to bill-discount only and cut the limit
realisation days past the agreed tenor or a shipping bill unpaid -> no renewal, ask for buyer-wise order confirmations
factory does not reopen on the announced date [2] or extends beyond the announced break [4] -> put on watchlist, hold renewal
one buyer crossing the share of sales you set at sanction (collect from customer the current split) -> require order confirmations per buyer and cap exposure
watch_note: Trigger levels are policy suggestions (analytical framing), not data.
